name: Playa Carmen
description: Playa Carmen is the beating heart of the area, the crossroads where the main coastal road meets the beach access. It concentrates supermarkets, restaurants, surf shops, banks and beach breaks, making it the most convenient and connected spot for a car-free nomad who wants everything close.
bestFor: First-timers and nomads who want everything within walking distance
pros: Best access to shops, banks and restaurants
cons: Busiest and dustiest part of town
Less peaceful than the outer areas

name: Santa Teresa Beach
description: Santa Teresa beach is the long, sunset-facing main strip running north from Playa Carmen, lined with beach clubs, yoga studios, boutique hotels, cafes and villas. It is the postcard heart of the scene, buzzing at golden hour, and home to much of the nomad and wellness community along its dusty spine.
bestFor: Surf-and-wellness nomads who want the full scene and social energy
pros: Best concentration of cafes, coworking and yoga
cons: Crowded and lively in high season

name: Playa Hermosa
description: Just north of the main strip, Playa Hermosa is a broad, mellow beach with a calmer, more spacious feel and excellent surf. It suits nomads who want the ocean and community within easy reach but prefer a quieter, less congested base away from the busiest central bustle.
bestFor: Surfers and nomads wanting a quieter beach with room to breathe
cons: Further from central shops and services

name: Malpais
description: South of Playa Carmen, Malpais keeps more of its original fishing-village character: quieter, more rustic and rugged, with rocky coves, tide pools and a slower pace. It draws those seeking calm and nature over nightlife, and sits closest to the Cabo Blanco nature reserve at the peninsula's tip.
bestFor: Nomads craving peace, nature and a slower rhythm
pros: Beautiful rocky coves and tide pools
